cohort: The study included published research comparing perinatal outcomes and risk factors in single versus twin pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM).
finding: Twin pregnancies complicated by GDM showed significantly higher risks for adverse maternal outcomes (e.g., preterm birth, preeclampsia, cesarean section) and neonatal outcomes (e.g., low birth weight, asphyxia, death) compared to single pregnancies with GDM.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates were significantly higher in the twin pregnancy group complicated by GDM.
